why: Rule 1 clean: deg-3 junction where a 176 cm MIP muon and two short protons all cool toward it, and p4 shows both protons rising monotonically away to their Bragg ends at 12001/12003.

21002 is the collinear trap (its two muon prongs are 1.5 degrees from straight with a 9.5 cm delta), but the cluster's free end 21001 is the real candidate: the zoom over z=-10..38 shows the argon upstream of it completely empty, so the muon starts there rather than entering the z=0 face, it leaves 15 degrees off the beam axis, it is cooler at 21001 (62k vs 70k) per rule 1, and a blob sits 2.8 cm off it transverse to the track.

Rule 8 territory: five isolated sub-cm dots with no fitted segment and no readable direction anywhere; 11000 is the only proton-level (~150k e/cm) deposit and sits at the centre of the tight three-dot group, which is the most I can say.

Rule 7 plus rule 1: in the principal frame the whole event opens out as a cone from a1=-50 and 18016 is at that narrow apex, with a 7.9 cm pi+ leaving it and stopping hot (108k) at 18001 while two e prongs head downstream into the widening shower.

Two independent stopping protons 65 cm apart (Bragg at 13000 and at 39026), so rule 1 is satisfied at both origins 13001 and 39025; I took 13001 because its proton carries ~6x the charge and its neighbourhood holds several more fragments, but rule 2 points the other way and this is close to a coin flip.

Rule 1: a 6.7 cm proton rises monotonically 90k to 250k away from 11002 to its Bragg end at 11001, and the 303 cm muon leaves 11002 at 98 degrees with no Bragg there before exiting the x- wall, so both prongs start at 11002.
Single 20.4 cm proton whose p4 profile peaks at 208k in the first 1.5 cm from the 14000 end and falls monotonically to 105k, so it stops at 14000 and its origin, the vertex, is the cool end 14002.

The whole event is one 3.4 cm heavily-ionising stub and it is hot at both ends with a cooler middle, so rule 1 gives no direction (tight zooms on 7001 and on 7000 both come back red, i.e. hotter at whichever end you stand on); I took the lower-z end on rule 2 alone and this is close to a coin flip.

Rule 1 at a 75 degree junction: the 217 cm muon and the 82 cm pi+ are both coolest at 7002 (60k and 58k) and both get hotter away from it, the pi+ following the stopping template up to 93k, and 7002 is also the lowest-z candidate.
Only a 2.8 cm hot stub in the event; the tight zoom shows dark red points at the 10001 end and blue at the 10000 end, so the particle stops at 10001 and by rule 1 the vertex is 10000.

Rule 1 fully satisfied, 2 of 2: the 17.7 cm proton rises monotonically 105k to 250k away from 10011 into a textbook Bragg at 10001, and the 160 cm muon is also cooler at 10011, with the prongs 129 degrees apart so not the collinear trap.

The 125 cm track's smooth monotone 140k-to-60k decay over the first 15 cm from 29008 is a real Bragg there (the spiky rise at the other end is contamination from the 4 cm 193k proton stub sitting on 29010), so the track originates at 29010, where two short hot proton stubs also start; the 395 cm cluster 22 is a separate vertical cosmic.

Textbook 3-prong star: the zoom shows cool cyan points right at 6003 with a 27 cm hadron Bragging to 235k at 6000, a 12.4 cm pi+ Bragging to 205k at 6001, and an 18 cm e prong, i.e. everything comes out of 6003.

Rule 1 2-of-2 plus rule 3: the 101 cm muon leaves 5003 flat at MIP and rises along the stopping-muon template to 165k at 5004 where a 9.6 cm Michel hangs off (so 5004 is the far end), while a 30.4 cm proton leaves 5003 and Braggs to 295k at 5000.

The 224 cm cluster-23 track is flat MIP end to end while skimming the y- floor from the z=500 corner, i.e. a through-going cosmic with no Bragg and no real Michel, leaving the 14.1 cm proton as the interaction; its charge rises monotonically 125k to 305k toward 34005, so the vertex is its cool origin 34004.
